T1640b|.|**A UNIFORM VALUE CANNOT CARRY AN ARRAY OF ROWS, SO GENERATORS UNROLL (the root the §B260 audit found under the Ramp, Grid Warp, the curve table and the Render's lights).** `UniformValue = number | boolean | readonly number[]` (`src/runtime/backend/plan.ts:21`): a pass's uniforms are named scalars and one flat vector each, so a table of rows becomes numbered members (`g0..g31`, `c0..c63`, `light{i}…`) and, in the Render, numbered CODE. the Ramp's docblock says so. wanted: a typed table as a uniform value (an array of structs with a run-time count beside it, written as one buffer region), or a small data-buffer resource a node can own, so a generator indexes rows in a loop; the three table nodes moved onto it; §V1029's gate then holds them flat. the lights do not wait for this (they take a storage buffer, §T1623b). the seam ruled for the lights (§T1623b slice 2: values for a region of a buffer, carried by the plan and written like a uniform block's) is this row's mechanism; the Ramp, Grid Warp and the curve table move onto it after the lights.|T1635b,B260,V1029
T1649b|.|**A BOARD THAT TAKES ONE COLUMN OR TWO BY THE WIDTH IT IS GIVEN, AND AN "ALL" VIEW ACROSS PANELS (owner, 2026-10-06, relayed by shaderloom-f1).** owner: *"i still would like an 'All' tab where we see all of them at once … and where there is space definitely 2 columns"*. the consumer built `panel_all` by hand: a second 16-column board repeating every member of its three Panels (a member on two Panels works; the banks join both by name), shipped with Phone off. what is asked of the app: (a) a board whose sections flow into one, two or more columns by the width of the surface showing it (desk pane, phone upright, phone sideways), so a project does not lay the same controls out twice; (b) an All view across the document's Panels on the desk and on the phone, made by the app, not authored. design first, with §T1610b's open items (pages are automatic from labels; a page with few columns has very large cells sideways; pages are derived on the phone only): what a board's authored grid means once the surface may re-flow it, and what stays where the author put it. ALSO THE OWNER, 2026-10-06 (relayed): *"the sliders for the controls could be a tiny bit less high on both app pane and on mobile. just a smidge too chunky"*. a board's row is as tall as its column is wide, so the column count is the only handle a project has on a control's height: the consumer went from eight columns to ten (`4bb29f77`) to make every control a little lower, re-gridding three boards. wanted in the same design: A ROW HEIGHT THAT IS NOT TIED TO THE COLUMN WIDTH (a number on the board, or a density the surface chooses), so "a little lower" is a value and not a re-layout.|T1607b,T1610b,T1517b,T1561b
T1648b|.|**A PRESET IS REMOVED AND RENAMED WHERE IT IS STORED, AND A BANK'S STRIP SAYS WHAT IT IS (owner, 2026-10-06, relayed by shaderloom-f1).** owner: *"how do we remove presets set in the controls?"* today: select the bank node, Inspector, Presets bank, Delete beside each; the board's strip has Store and no Delete, and the owner had made presets from the strip's Store. wanted on the DESK board's strip: delete and rename beside Store (one undoable command each; a deleted preset that a cue or a morph names says so before it goes), and a caption for the strip (the bank's role, by `surfaceNameOf`) so a row of names reads as what it is. the PHONE keeps its rule: it recalls, it never stores or deletes.|T1619b,T1517b,T1561b
T1647b|.|**PHONE: SCROLLING WITHOUT MOVING A SLIDER, SECOND ATTEMPT, DECIDED IN THE OWNER'S HAND (§T1609b failed on a real phone, 2026-10-06).** owner: *"also still pretty hard to not screw with the sliders when scrolling on mobile"*. §T1607b made the WHOLE WIDTH of every slider hot (relative drag from anywhere after 12 px along it), reasoned from Chromium's rules and WebKit's source and never held in a hand; a thumb's scroll starts on a slider nearly every time and often sideways enough to be taken. candidates, each an established answer: (K) THE KNOB ONLY — a slider follows a touch that starts on its thumb, as a native iOS slider does, and the rest of the track scrolls; (H) HOLD TO GRAB — a control follows only after the finger rests on it for a moment, a moving finger always scrolls; (L) A LOCK — the page is in scroll mode or play mode by one switch that is always in reach; (G) A GUTTER — a strip of every board is never a control (the consumer's layout stopgap, made the page's own). a design from reading has failed once, so THIS ROW IS DECIDED BY TRYING: the candidates are built behind one setting on the phone page, the owner tries each on the phone in one sitting, one stays and the rest are deleted with the setting. acceptance is the owner's word, then the touch-emulated spec for the chosen rule. also here: `phone-touch.spec.ts` reads the consumer's live Panels (edited twice by the consumer's session for its own layout changes) — it gets a frozen fixture of its own, as the bore test did. **BUILT AND ON MAIN FOR THE OWNER TO TRY: the frozen fixture `df5ee75d`, the trial `35845323` (the worker's runs: `phone-page.test.ts` 145, the seven phone test files 245, the touch spec 23 of 23 twice, the gates 3,607; the lead's verification of the landing is recorded with the next entry).** ONE CORE: a slider, fader or pad takes a touch after 12 px of travel its way, then moves by the travel; a MODE only says what must be true before that. ONE TRIAL CONTROL at the right end of the phone's tab bar, two lines, "Touch K" and "Rows 36", each the phone's own picker, kept per phone in `localStorage` (`loom.phone.trial`); every line of it is marked "T1647b trial … deleted when the owner has chosen". THE MODES: K THE KNOB ONLY (default) — the touch must land on the knob, drawn 56 px wide (about 9 mm, the thumb target of Parhi, Karlson and Bederson 2006) and kept whole at both ends; the rest of the track scrolls; a pad follows only from its puck and scrolls from everywhere else, so it needs no rail. H HOLD TO GRAB — the finger rests 200 ms within 8 px and the outline arrives; a finger that moves sooner is let go for that touch. L A LOCK — a Play / Scroll switch at the left end of the tab bar; in Scroll the board takes no touch and is dimmed; starts in Play each visit. G A STRIP — 56 px down the right or the left edge that always scrolls, the board inset beside it. A as §T1607b, to compare. K+G and K+H (a 100 ms rest) as one table row each. ROWS: 32, 36 or 44 px, default 36 (§B269). IN EMULATION every mode keeps its own promise: a board three screens tall flicked top to bottom and back from sliders, with flicks that start fast or hesitant, on the knob or beside it, wrote nothing; in K a drag from 4 px outside the drawn knob does nothing and a drag from the knob moves by travel with no jump. NOTHING HERE HAS BEEN HELD IN A HAND: whether a real thumb lands on a 56 px knob while scrolling, rests 200 ms, or wanders is the whole question and the owner's sitting answers it; iOS Safari in every mode is unverified. known rough edges: the trial control takes 72 px of the tab bar (a fourth tab's name elides at 375 px); in K the knob's outline is drawn over the caption's chip. the numbered recipe went to the owner 2026-10-06. **2026-10-07 Android/Chrome report: a default K drag could be cancelled before script capture when its initial movement was diagonal. The visible slider/fader knob now has hit testing and touch-action:none, like the XY puck; the bare track remains pan-y. A touch on the knob belongs to the control and cannot scroll the page, while off-knob touches scroll without writes. No touchdown write and the existing relative-drag threshold remain. The unexpected All/Scene/Camera section-pager row was removed; one Panel-tab row and the authored section headings/layout remain. Trial modes are otherwise unchanged; physical-device rechecking remains required.**|T1609b,T1607b,T1610b,T1561b
T1646b|.|**A COMPILED NODE HAS NO WAY TO RAISE A PROBLEM ON ONE FRAME AND NOT THE NEXT (found by §T1589b slice 2; the same gap §T1641b's inventory named: per-frame warnings have no reader).** a diagnostic that depends on a VALUE (a Light's Type driven to Spot in Single mode, a Range driven to zero, a count driven past a capacity) can only be said by the structural compile, which runs on a revision; `compileFrame` drops every recompiled node's diagnostics and only the value graph's own source is per-frame. wanted: a per-frame problem carrier for compiled nodes (a seam in `frame-compile.ts` and the app's frame loop, read by the Problems registry and by the headless harness), rate-limited so a value crossing a threshold every frame does not flood, with the rule for when a value-dependent problem appears and clears. the first use goes away with §T1623b slice 3 (a named Light becomes a row and a spot is a kind); the always-walked-rows warning of §T1623b is the second and stays. a third case (§T1652b's lane, 2026-10-06): a finding that a value causes two or more hops away through channels (a clamp far downstream of a slider) is no longer said at the write, since the values lane does not resolve the whole downstream of a channel; it is said at the next structural revision. the per-frame carrier would say it at once. **2026-10-06, from §T1652b's lane boundary (`802f9326`):** a frameless finding such as `parameter.expression.clamped` on a node that reads the written value through ANOTHER node's channel is now said at the next structural revision, not on the write.|T1589b,T1641b,T1623b
T1645b|.|**A NOTICE STILL RESIZES THE PANES: WHERE "OUTPUT STALE" LIVES (left by §B265; the owner's call).** since §B265 a notice takes its room from the foot of the window and no pane's top edge moves, but pane HEIGHTS still change when one toggles (the canvas 784 ↔ 815 px; the bottom dock's tab strip moves about 31 px), and "Output stale" toggles on every add-a-node-then-wire-it cycle. two ways to remove the twitch, neither built: (a) a permanently reserved one-line status row at the foot (31 px always spent, nothing ever moves); (b) "Output stale" as a chip in a row that already exists, as the shader pane does for its own stale mark (`dock-panes.tsx`, `.shaderStale`), the strip kept for notices that hold a decision — §T1121 chose the full sentence in the strip on purpose. also here: the node library's "compatible with … clear" banner pushes its list down a row when a wire is picked up; and the wire snap's first-connection frames (7 in 0.72 s) because the snap plays over the node's first compile.|B265,T1121,T1639b
T1644b|.|**THE WIRE SNAP: WHAT §T1639b PROPOSES AND DID NOT BUILD.** (1) THE NODE NUDGE: in the reference the target node is pushed about 10 px away from the wire at the snap, peaking at 130 ms and back by 400 ms; left out because it moves the node's box (§V389) — the owner's ruling, and if yes, as a transform on a visual layer that the box gates do not read. (2) a "this input is fed" mark: a hollow dot for an unfed input and a filled one for a fed input (Loom's analogue of the reference's dot fill), no tick and no new row chrome. (3) the nearest ACCEPTING port wins the range: today the library picks the closest handle whatever it is, so a nearer refusing port shadows a farther accepting one; needs hit-testing beside the library. (4) the strike: the reference's first arc on entering range is larger. (5) the snap for connections made ELSEWHERE (an agent, the Connections panel, undo and redo): only hand gestures on the canvas play it. (6) Escape cancels a pulled wire. (7) the look checked in Safari and Firefox, above 100 % zoom, inside a component dive, and with a finger on a real device.|T1639b,V389
T1638b|.|**A POINTSET'S `swap` SPLITS THE RENDER'S RUN: N GEOMETRIES ARE N DEVICE PASSES IN THE LAST TARGET DRAWN (found by §T1587b slice 2, on §T1604b's ground; derived and counted, not changed).** each pointset's `swap` is emitted after its last reader, which puts it between two Geometries' draws, and a swap ends a run (`renderPassRuns`). ten Geometries of ten pointsets: the shadow cube is one run of 61 draws, but the lit target (or the Normal layer when it is drawn last) is ten runs of one. moving the swaps after the Render's last draw would make the counted cases 2 and 5 device passes instead of 11 and 14. wanted: the swaps of pointsets a Render reads hoisted past its last draw (say what a later reader in the same frame then sees), with `render-pass-runs.test.ts` counting it. with §T1615b (3), the same class: a dispatch landing inside a run. also (§T1589b slice 1): in `encodeSegmented` a swap counts as work a dispatch would overtake, so every kernel in a frame costs one more encoder and one more submit — on the consumer four more dispatches were six more submits. same fix: the swaps hoisted, and counted.|T1604b,T1615b,T1587b
T1587b|.|**SWEEP / EXTRUDE — OPEN; sheets, endpoint tangent correction and UV slice 2b landed.** Deliverable: ring/square/strip/custom profile swept over curves into lit grid surfaces with caps/twist/per-point radius/scale and G-buffer outputs. Preserve the complete D decisions/consumer C contract in the linked record and `docs/sweep-design-2026-10-05.md`. Current sheet claim is grid:{cols}x{rows}x{sheets}, wraps afterward; one sheet keeps the old claim, slot = (sheet × rows + row) × cols + col, and no cell joins sheets. One vertex-pulled draw/emitter; ctx.dim describes one sheet and adds sheet/sheets; kernels retain properly lit sheet topology. UV reaches stock material and tiles by Map Extend (T1618b). OPEN: Beam draws a strip (T1586b slice 5); C11 custom outline by length; C12 longer typed table or CPU formula-path reader; C14 a port stating one strip with a frame. Recorded unchecked cases remain SSAA/projector/environment/AO, asserted sheet MSAA, degenerate capped strips and all-degenerate 37,000-point cost; tiny grid normals’ +Z fallback was found but not fixed here. Historical timing predates the reference-pass rule; use controlled measurement on resume. [Full original contract, decisions and evidence](SPEC-ARCHIVE.md#archive-2026-10-09-t1587b).|T1561b,T1586b
T1588b|.|**AN OBJECT TRANSFORM ON SCENE GEOMETRY (proposed by shaderloom-f1, same doc).** both products put a transform, a look-at and a parent on every 3D object. Loom's `geometry` refuses a non-identity orient (`scene.ts` ~855–880) and the working idiom is a point kernel that rewrites every vertex each frame to move a rigid hull (the furnace rig; sentinel-bot's body: 87,751 vertices per robot per frame). wanted: translate, rotate, scale and pivot with the order stated, a look-at target and a parent, applied as the draw's MODEL MATRIX in every pass (colour, G-buffer, shadows); composes with the instance transform of §T1581b, so it is designed in that row's design doc. 1st in the ruled build order, with §T1581b. T1625b|.|**A CONE AGAINST A CELL (accepted limitation 4 of §T1589b's design, `docs/lights-from-pointset-design-2026-10-06.md` section 9).** A spot is culled by its range sphere. T1599b|.|**A SOCKET APPEARS ONLY WHEN IT APPLIES (from §T1581b).** the Geometry's "Shape Mesh" input is read only in Instances mode with Shape: Mesh, yet it is drawn on every Geometry and makes each one a port row taller (E13 needed 16 px). §V122 hides parameters that do not apply; ports have no such rule. wanted: a port-level `inactiveWhen` — the node box, the canvas, connect and the layout rule (§V389) all treat a hidden port as absent; decide what happens to an existing wire when its port stops applying (keep it and show it dimmed with a named warning, or refuse the mode change by name), and how TouchDesigner treats an unused input. then the Shape Mesh socket uses it. the same class (§T1589b slice 1): a Light in Single mode with its Points input wired keeps the upstream kernel dispatching every frame, read by nothing — an input a mode does not read must not keep its producer alive.|T1581b,V122,V389,V372
T1608b|.|**ADDITIVE GEOMETRY: ALPHA AND DRAW ORDER DIFFER BY MODE (found fixing §B256, not changed).** (1) an additive billboard, quad or box ADDS ITS ALPHA over a transparent background, an additive Surface adds none — measured: `[0,0,0,0]` becomes `[0,0,0,255]` under a black additive quad, so such a glow composited over another layer cuts a black shape. T1610b|.|**PHONE PAGE: WHAT §T1607b DECIDED ALONE AND THE OWNER MAY OVERRULE, AND WHAT IT LEFT OUT.** (1) the momentary Button's hold starts 150 ms late and a held finger that slides far enough to scroll lets go; the alternative is an immediate press and no scrolling from buttons — a per-control choice if both are wanted. (4) pages are automatic from labels, so the shipped Scene Panel shows All / Scene / Camera with no opt-out. (5) SIDEWAYS: the pager's 52 px row is a seventh of the screen and a page with few columns has very large square cells. (6) no pages for legacy text-layout Panels. (7) pages are derived on the phone only; the desk has no such view. each needs the owner's hands on §T1609b first. T1609b|.|**PHONE PANEL SCROLLING ON A REAL PHONE — THE OWNER'S LIVE TEST (§T1607b was verified in headless Chromium only).** iOS Safari and Android Chrome are unrun. the questions a device answers: (a) iPhone: while dragging a slider, does a finger that wanders up or down make the page scroll and the slider let go (WebKit's late cancel)? if so the value must stay and a second touch continue from it; (b) a 45° start becomes a scroll or a drag, never both — which, per phone; (c) Android's slop is the platform's, not the emulation's 15 px: does the 12 px take still feel immediate; (d) a drag from the very left edge against Safari's back swipe; (e) the page jumping when Safari's toolbars hide; (f) sideways, whether two navigation rows leave room on Scene. the numbered recipe (18 steps, sentinel's three Panels) was handed to the owner 2026-10-06. **THE OWNER TRIED IT ON A REAL PHONE, 2026-10-06 (relayed by shaderloom-f1): A FAIL.** *"also still pretty hard to not screw with the sliders when scrolling on mobile"*. the direction lock and relative drag of §T1607b are not enough in the hand. the consumer's stopgap is layout: every control on its phone panels takes six columns of eight, leaving the right quarter bare to scroll from. the redesign is §T1647b; this row closes when the owner's hand says so.|T1607b
T1606b|.|**SHADOW CASTERS: WHAT §T1598b LEFT.** (1) a per-light `visible_<light>` list for INSTANCED geometry (weigh after §T1604b: an indirect draw costs ~0.05 ms per device pass today); (2) reach for directional lights (a sphere against the shadow box); (3) a bound from other producers (a grid, a Point Transform, a kernel that declares one) and a tighter shape than a sphere — a floor's sphere holds any light standing on it, so a floor is in all six faces; (4) the pipeline inspector does not show that a draw is skipped this frame. CONSUMER DATA POINT (shaderloom-f1, 2026-10-06, `2bc870d4`): item (3) is what would put the tunnel lamps' shadows back in sentinel-bot's live tier — the robot is 645,000 triangles of kernel-placed instances with nothing to cull by, so every cube face draws all of it (about 3.9 million triangles a light); a bound for kernel-placed instances lets a face skip them. see also §T1620b.|T1598b,T1604b,T1592b
T1605b|.|**THE KALEIDOSCOPE STARTER COMPONENT READS TWO LFOS OF ITS HOST DOCUMENT (found by §T1593b's equivalence check).** its inner `facets` reads `op('driftx1')` and `op('drifty1')`, nodes that exist only in the document the component was saved from; in the two on-nothing documents that embed it those references name nothing. a component that only drifts beside two particular nodes is not a component. wanted: the component owns its two LFOs (or publishes two inputs for them), the starter is regenerated, and a gate fails a starter component whose graph references a name outside itself.|T1593b,T1221
T1620b|.|**A SHADOW-ONLY CASTER: A GEOMETRY THAT IS IN A LIGHT'S LIST BUT NOT IN THE LIT PASS (proposed by shaderloom-f1 from sentinel-bot's live tier, 2026-10-06).** a cube shadow draws the lit geometry itself: the robot's 645,000 triangles six times a light. the other engines let a low-polygon stand-in cast for a dense object (TouchDesigner: a Geometry COMP's Render flag off with a light's Shadow Casters naming it; Notch: per-object Visible / Cast Shadows flags — CHECK both against the docs before designing, neither is read yet). wanted: a Geometry (or a flag on it) that casts and is not drawn in colour, Depth or Normal, and its counterpart, a lit Geometry that does not cast; named in caster lists like any other (§T1598b); a diagnostic when a stand-in casts for nothing that is lit. design note with the TD/Notch comparison first. the consumer can also cut its kit (the ring is 716 triangles, 540 times), which this does not replace.|T1598b,T1606b,T1561b
T1637b|.|**ROPE: MANY SHORT STRANDS ARE THROUGHPUT-BOUND (R18 of §T1585b, measured in slice 1).** a million points as 18,181 strands of 55 cost 1.43–1.50 ms a step against 0.44 ms for a plain kernel over the same points: one invocation a strand walks its points through storage reads and writes. wanted: function-local arrays for strands under a length, so a short strand is solved in registers and written once; measured with a reference pass (§B260).|T1585b
T1636b|.|**THE BACKEND WRITES STEP UNIFORMS BY NAME INTO ANY BLOCK OF A STEPPED DISPATCH, AND NOTHING RESERVES THE NAMES (R19 of §T1585b, found by a test in slice 1).** a member called `iterations`, `substep`, `seed` (and the others the region writer knows) in a stepped dispatch's uniform block is overwritten each step with the region's value; the Rope's own Newton cap was named `iterations` and silently read 1. the Rope has a definition test; every other node that declares kernel steps is unguarded, and a Custom kernel's author can collide without knowing. wanted, as a seam fix and not a per-node test: ONE list of the names the region writer owns, a refusal by name at compile when a definition or an author's Params declares one for another meaning (the Render's `SURFACE_RESERVED_NAMES` is the idiom), and a gate over every definition that declares steps.|T1585b,T1583b
T1635b|.|**GENERATED SHADER TEXT MUST NOT GROW WITH A COUNT THE DOCUMENT DECIDES: THE AUDIT, THE RULE AND ITS GATE (owner, 2026-10-06, on §B260: *"we do the real cure right so it becomes a core fix of the whole app and not an inplace shader trick of a single patch"*).** §B260 is one instance of a shape: N generated blocks, one per document item, combined in one function. THE CURE FOR LIGHTS is one light path (§T1623b: every light is a row in the Render's light table walked by one loop, casting lights included through an indexable shadow resource, so the lit text holds no light and a change of light count recompiles nothing); its design is the last section of `docs/light-cost-investigation-2026-10-06.md`, reviewed before it is built. THE REST OF THE APP: an audit of every generator for text or plan structure that grows with a document count (projectors, environments, layer stacks and N-input compositing, fused effect chains, kernel attributes and steps, instance attributes, Group predicates, preview synthesis), each classed as §B260-shaped, compile-time only, pass-count only or bounded, with the largest count any shipped document reaches — `docs/generated-text-growth-audit-2026-10-06.md`, LANDED `19a69805` (read from the generators, then measured in TEXT through the real `compileGraph` at N = 1, 2, 4, 16; all 112 shipped documents compiled; no GPU run). THE RULE becomes an invariant (§V1029, reserved): counts are data, not text; exceptions are listed with a bound and a reason. THE GATE is on the cause, not a clock: each generator's text derived at several counts, identical or within a declared ledger whose bounds can only go down. also from §B260: the reference-pass timing harness becomes a tool of the test harness. **WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND:** THE §B260 SHAPE EXISTS IN FOUR PLACES, ALL IN `src/nodes/shaders/scene-render.wgsl.ts`, none bounded: R1 the Surface generator's light blocks (PBR 1,956 bytes a light, `fs` 121,482 bytes at 64; largest shipped 13); R2 the instances generator's own copy of the light block (primitive instances, billboards, beams; largest shipped 3); R3 projector blocks appended to the same `lit` in both (1,261 bytes plain, 1,851 with cookie and occlusion; largest shipped 5; their additions sit under two `if`s, which §B260 measured as keeping them out of the cliff); R4 a casting light's shadow lookup inside its block (4,012 bytes directional, 4,140 point; bounded only by 16 sampled textures a stage; largest shipped 6 casting). the largest shipped chain is 14 blocks and 30 `lit +=` in one 38,685-byte `fs` (on-nothing/title), the longest function in any shipped plan. a light-count change today recompiles every lit text of every Render that lists it (worst shipped: sentinel-bot, 4 lit texts, 154 KB). BOUNDED CHAIN: Composite's fold (`acc = blendPixel(acc, sample)` a layer, 139 bytes and a binding each, refused past 8 by `node.compile.tooManyInputs`). ON PURPOSE: `PERLIN_4_CORNERS`, 16 unrolled blocks, a definition constant. EVERYTHING ELSE grows as declarations, independent statements or passes sharing a text (point kernel 426 bytes and 2 functions an attribute; compaction 311; Render geometries 0 text and up to 12 passes each). THE DATA FORM ALREADY EXISTS in the app: the Cache / Echo / Slit Scan ring (one `texture_2d_array` and a uniform), loop regions for substeps and kernel steps — text byte-identical across counts, measured. WHY ROWS GET UNROLLED: `UniformValue = number | boolean | readonly number[]` (`runtime/backend/plan.ts`) cannot carry an array of rows; the Ramp, Grid Warp (`g0..g31`) and the curve table (`c0..c63`) work round it with numbered members (§T1640b). small waste: the shadow matte declares and binds every shadow map though it reads three. THE RULE IS §V1029, as proposed with one addition by the lead (exception (d): a bounded chain of 8 or fewer under a named refusal with a linear-cost measurement on record — Composite; kernel attributes' byte bound counts as a stated count). THE GATE AS FIRST DESIGNED: 106 count axes derived from the registry (15 variadic ports, 23 pointset inputs, 52 compile-time numbers, 16 code parameters), a positive control first (it must class today's `render.lights` as a chain at 1,888 bytes an item), cost a few seconds, no GPU. not read by the audit: `src/runtime/backend/vgpu/**`, document sources and project shaders (author WGSL can write the same shape; the gate does not see it). **THE GATE LANDED `f5fa2e85` (+ `17b6aaac`: the instruction files count 58 gate files; verified on main: typecheck; the new file with `generated-text`, `scene-light-guard`, `gate-list` 47; the worker ran the gates once, 58 files / 3,573).** `src/compiler/generated-text-growth.test.ts`, 26 tests, 2.1–2.5 s under vitest, no GPU: 127 count axes DERIVED over 153 definitions (the five classes plus a sixth the derivation needed, compile-time STRING parameters — Group predicates, Instance Attributes, Mesh File In's Lamps are lists written in strings), 141 ledger rows, all 17 `generatedOnce` generators run under some row; compiled at 1, 2, 4, 15, 16 so the numbers are taken on two unit steps (the second item and the last). `NOT_YET_DATA` (all §T1623b, exact sizes that can only move by an edit): `render.lights` a chain through `lit`, `fs` +1,885 a light (+1,924 for the sixteenth with the stopgap's guard), unbounded; the same in the instances generator +1,823; casting +3,860 directional and +3,835 point, bounded at 16 by `compiler/binding-budget`; `render.projectors` +971 plain and +1,447 with cookie and occlusion. exception (d): Composite's six blend axes, a chain through `acc`, +82 and a binding an input, refused past 8 — MEASUREMENT OWED. Switch is NOT a chain (a `switch` arm carries nothing): statements, bounded at 8. exception (a) has its own derived list: every node's minimal graph is compiled and any function writing one accumulation more than 8 times outside a loop must be named — it finds only `perlin4`, 16 times (the next largest in the catalogue is 6). the Rope's only axis is flat; sheets is a branch. RED THREE WAYS by editing: a row removed; a chain's length changed by one; a flat axis made to grow (`lightCount` fed from the geometry count: "THE TEXT OF ONE ITEM NOW CARRIES lit ACROSS ITEMS"); ten more lies are permanent tests. OWED, printed by the gate without failing: (1) Composite's linear-cost measurement with a reference pass; (2) FIVE AXES GROW PER AUTHOR STRUCT FIELD WITH NO REFUSAL AT ANY COUNT — a kernel's Params fields (2), Material · WGSL's Params, Instance fields and Instance Attributes: under exception (b) they need a named refusal at a stated count (the uniform block's size limit as a diagnostic by name would do). WHAT THE GATE CANNOT SEE: author WGSL and the document sources that build it with loops of their own; cost (it asserts form, never time); a value carried through a pointer argument or an array write; one node's count as a literal in another node's text; a fixed chain only a non-default mode emits. STILL OPEN IN THIS ROW: the two OWED items; the reference-pass timing harness as a tool of the test harness; then it closes when §T1623b empties `NOT_YET_DATA`.|B260,T1623b,T1589b
T1634b|.|**CONTROL RESET: WHAT §T1619b's DESIGN LEAVES OUT (section 6 of `docs/control-reset-design-2026-10-06.md`).** (1) a Layer's fader and switch on a board reset too (a Layer is not a control node; its opacity's default is the type's). (2) reset with a time: Reset cuts; a fade home needs a morph record, and records live in a bank. (3) a phone undoes its own last press (undo is per actor, §V41, and the phone page has no door to its stack); with one, Reset all could stop asking. (4) reset one page of a paged board (pages are derived on the phone, §T1610b (7)). (5) the reset sheet lists what is away, each row resetting one control: the route with no gesture and the only one for assistive technology (§T1611b). (6) sentinel-bot takes its defaults from its table and its three `saved` banks go (§T1561b, the consumer's own change). (7) a published component parameter has an authored default, as a TouchDesigner custom parameter has. (8) a hardware button resets: MIDI learn onto `control.reset`. (9) DESK SLIDERS JUMP, PHONE SLIDERS DO NOT: `useDrag` in `src/editor/controls/control-widget.tsx` writes on `pointerdown`, the phone has been relative since §T1607b — decide whether the desk takes the relative rule. (10) agent tools for the two commands.|T1619b
T1619b|.|**RESET A CONTROL, OR ALL OF THEM, TO WHAT WAS SAVED — ON THE DESK AND ON THE PHONE (owner, 2026-10-06, relayed by shaderloom-f1).** owner: *"ways to reset controls individually or all according to what was saved or something should be something useful accessible on both phone and browser"*. what exists: a Presets bank on a Panel is drawn on both, so "all" can be authored today as a preset holding every control's shipped value (sentinel-bot does, `2bc870d4`: three banks `presets_robot|scene|lights`, one preset `saved` each; `panels.test.ts` moves every control and recalls). what does not exist: (a) ONE control back to its saved value, by a gesture that cannot be made by accident now that touch is relative (§T1607b): a double tap, a long press, or a small reset mark on the control; (b) "saved" as a thing the document knows without an author writing a preset: the value in the file as last saved, or a snapshot taken by a "Set as default" action — a preset written by hand goes stale the moment a slider's shipped value changes; (c) a Panel-level "Reset all" that needs no bank. decide which "saved" it is first; (a) and (c) follow from it. acceptance on both surfaces: move a slider, reset it, it reads the saved value and ONE write went out; a scroll or a drag never resets. **DESIGN LANDED `59d90319` (`docs/control-reset-design-2026-10-06.md`); three questions go to the owner, the lead builds on the recommendations unless overruled.** WHICH "SAVED": a DEFAULT stored on the control in the document and moved only by "Set as default" on the desk — what TouchDesigner custom parameters, TouchOSC (`Default`, `Default Pull`), Open Stage Control and Notch keep. it starts as the value in the file through a one-time definition `migrate` (Slider, Toggle, XY Pad to definition version 2; no `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump), and `parametersFor` makes the inspector's existing "Reset to default" mean the same number. the alternative, the file as opened, already exists as `parameter.revert` (§T1184) but MOVES BY ITSELF: performed values are written on every save and autosave, so a reload or a crash mid-show makes wherever the sliders were the new "saved". (the row's first text was wrong about TouchOSC: it has no double-tap-to-default property; the built-in double-tap reset is Open Stage Control's `doubleTap`.) GESTURES, one rule: nothing resets from one press. PHONE: a DOUBLE TAP on a slider or pad (each tap ends in `pointerup` inside the control within 300 ms, under 10 px of travel, never taken by the control, not on a page still scrolling; the second within 300 ms and 32 px; fires on the second lift); a toggle has no gesture (a tap is its reset; a dot shows when it is off its default); Button, bank, cue list and Layer do not reset. DESK: right-click opens a short `control` menu (Reset, Set as default, Reset all on this Panel, Set all as default on this Panel) — not double-click, which the owner removed from number fields (§T1033) and which would write two moves first on a desk slider; one keymap entry and palette entries. SEEN: a tick on the track (a ring on the pad) at the default, brighter while the value is away; on the phone a dot on a Panel's tab. RESET ALL: phone, a ↺ in the tab bar with a count opens a sheet that asks once (a phone has no undo), the shown Panel only; desk, a ↺ in the Controls tab header, one undo group, no question. Set as default is desk only: no phone write can reach it. THE WRITE: two DOMAIN commands, `control.reset` and `control.setDefault`, `{ nodeIds } | { all: true }`, one patch, one undo group, one audit entry each, registered where `preset.recall` is so the headless server has them; the phone sends one POST `{ handle, values: { reset: true }, phase: "commit" }`; the snapshot gains each control's default. SLICES: S1 the default and the two commands (definition shape changes; E81 and E82 are the shipped examples with controls; presets skip the default keys); S2 the desk; S3 the phone's wire; S4 the phone page (`phone-touch.spec.ts`; the real-phone check joins §T1609b). FOUND: "Reset to default" on a Slider's Value gives 0.5 whatever its range (§T1184's pattern on controls; S1's `parametersFor` fixes it); `resetValue` in `src/ui/controls/drag-math.ts` has had no production caller since §T1033. what is left out is §T1634b; a defect found on the way is §B261. NOT STARTED: waits for a building slot behind §B260. **THE OWNER ASKED AGAIN, 2026-10-06 (relayed by shaderloom-f1):** *"resetting in the controls is not visible for me anywhere … i have to reload right now if i screw something up. want to be able reset individual controls or all page or all"*. the three design questions went to the owner and are unanswered; by standing instruction the lead builds on the recommendations (DEFAULT as the saved value; a double tap on the phone; Reset all asks first on the phone). also from the consumer: its reset presets were named `saved` and did not read as a reset (renamed `reset_robot`, `reset_all`), and a bank's strip on a board says nothing about what the bank is (§T1648b). S1 IN BUILD. **S1 LANDED `b533dfc2` (verified on main: typecheck; `control-default-commands`, `presets/commands`, `controls`, `bus`, `parameter-controls`, the consumer's `panels.test.ts` 87; `phone-touch.spec.ts` 9 of 9; the 26 catalogue walkers 447; `pnpm test:first-import` 282; the gates 60 files / 3,608; the worker ran 41 named files 763, the two examples' claims on Dawn 20, the build).** Slider, Toggle and XY Pad store `defaultValue`, `defaultOn`, `defaultX`, `defaultY` (definition version 2 with a `migrate`: default := stored value; no `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump); `parametersFor` makes the stored default the value key's schema default, so the inspector's "Reset to default" on a Slider goes to the slider's own default instead of 0.5. TWO DOMAIN COMMANDS in `src/domain/commands/control-default-commands.ts`, registered by `createDomainBus`: `control.reset` and `control.setDefault`, `{ nodeIds } | { all: true }` parsed by the bus, a Panel's id naming its members; one patch, one audit entry, one undo group, split from a drag's transaction; a driven key is left alone and named; nothing to change is refused by name. `control.fromParameter` writes the default, so a control made from a parameter is born at it. `controls.ts` exports `controlDefaultState(node)` (defaults, current, away, driven) for S2 and S3; "away" is further than 1/10000 of the range. §B261 FIXED IN THE SAME FEW LINES: one table, `CONTROL_STATE_KEYS` read through `presetHolds` — a whole-control preset holds only what a hand moves, a key named outright is still stored, a default is never stored and never recalled. E81 and E82 regenerated (the builder writes the registry's current definition version, so `sync.test.ts` was red until they were; 16 lines, defaults authored in both sources). the two commands have NO DOOR yet: two `COMMANDS_WITH_NO_INVOKER` entries marked "sliced on purpose" name S2 and S3, and that gate fails the day either gets an invoker. six diagnostic codes have rows in the class table. TO KNOW: a code-built document's builder now writes version-2 controls, and a control whose source authors NO default reads 0.5 clamped into its range — sentinel-bot's source must author its defaults (its committed file, version 1, migrates correctly when opened); S2 makes a missing default a refusal by name and a gate, not a silent 0.5. node migration runs on the root graph at load only, so a control inside a saved component definition is not migrated (Ramp v2 has the same limit). the "which keys are the value" table still exists in four other places (`control-widget.tsx`, `midi-controls.ts`, the phone's `READ_KEYS` and `PHONE_WRITABLE_KEYS`). a whole-Button preset still captures `held` and `presses`. S2 (THE DESK) IN BUILD. **S2, THE DESK, LANDED `4d63f6ff` (+ `91e146bb`; verified on main: typecheck; `control-default-commands`, `control-reset`, the class gate, `menus/schemas`, `bus` 111; headless e2e `control-reset.spec.ts` and `phone-touch.spec.ts` 25; the gates 62 files / 3,629 — after the lead removed a ledger line that was stale at the landing; the worker ran 74 named files 1,318, the catalogue walkers 451, the two examples' claims 40, the build). screenshots from the real app went to the owner.** THE MARK: two notches at a slider's default at the top and bottom of its track (never across the caption or the value), a ring on the pad, a corner dot on a toggle off its default; bright in the text colour while away. ONE CONTROL: a right-click opens the `control` menu (a new menus-as-data surface): Reset, Set as default, Reset all on the Panel, Set all as default on the Panel; a row that could only refuse is greyed with the command's own sentence; on a control's own canvas node the widget gives the control menu and the rest of the node the node menu. S3 and S4 (the phone) wait for the owner's choice of touch mode (§T1647b).|T1607b,T1610b,T1517b,T1561b
T1660b|.|**A PORT CANNOT TAKE A NAME FROM ITS NODE'S OWN VALUES.** a Material · WGSL that declares `// @texture lens` shows "Texture 1" on the canvas socket and in the inspector's Connections list, because a port's label comes from the node TYPE. showing "Texture 1 · lens" needs per-node port labels in the node contract (what `parametersFor` is for parameters), read by the canvas, the inspector, the wire tooltip and the agent's `get_node`. the same seam would serve Custom WGSL · Multi's named inputs and a component's sockets. not hooked into the editor for one node type, on purpose.|T1658b
T1661b|.|**A `notYet` FINDING THAT LEAVES THE PLAN USABLE.** a Material · WGSL with a named texture and no wire withdraws the whole plan (§T1658b), as Custom WGSL · Multi does: the class gate allows `local` on `never` rows only. while a wire is being made the picture goes away. making it local needs a stand-in the node draws with (a named texture reads as transparent black, as live media with no source does) and the gate's rule on `local` widened with its reason; decide once for every node of this shape, not per node.|T1658b,T1641b
T1662b|.|**NO MIP LEVELS ON A MATERIAL'S TEXTURE.** `// @use map` reads by `textureLoad` (there is no sampler in a draw pass), so a picture minified on a surface far from the camera aliases; the input descriptions say so. needs either a sampler binding in the Render's draws (a binding of the 16) or a level chosen by the material from the derivative of its coordinate over a mip chain built upstream (the Mipmap node's output). measure which on the consumer's shape (the robots' eye lenses are small on screen).|T1658b
T1657b|.|**A NAMED LIGHT WITH A RANGE THAT COVERS THE PICTURE COSTS MORE AS A ROW THAN IT DID AS A BLOCK (found by §T1623b slice 3; the same pictures to the byte).** 16 lights of Range 30 on the floor: blocks 0.94–1.02 of the reference against rows 1.45–1.48; 64: 4.05–4.30 against 5.70–6.22. a row found through a cell reads four rows and tests a cone it mostly has not; where a light does not reach, a row costs a read and a compare, which is the grid's whole point. one shipped document has such Lights (the consumer's three) and its frame did not move. the cure is the one that worked for the always-walked rows: a cell's rows split by kind, two passes over a cell's words. measure on a document that has many ranged named Lights before building.|T1623b,T1625b
T1659b|.|**PREVIEW CAMERA CONTROLS: WHAT §T1655b's WALK LEFT.** (1) a stock-scene tile whose node only READS a moving value (a light tinted by a slider, any expression on time) stays on the last edit's values: refusing the values lane there would send every such slider down the structural road; the fix is the lane re-deriving rows from the payloads it already captures. T1654b|.|**FOUND BY §T1619b S2, NOT ITS OWN.** (1) THE PALETTE RUNS EVERY COMMAND WITH EMPTY INPUT: a command that needs the selection (Delete, Bypass, Duplicate, `control.reset`) is listed and refuses; wanted: the palette resolves an entry's input from the keymap environment, as a key press does. T1651b|.|**A SAMPLE-AND-HOLD VALUE NODE (asked by shaderloom-f1 for sentinel-bot's director, 2026-10-06).** wanted: a value node that takes `value` and a `trigger` (a rising edge, or a count that changed) and publishes the value as it was at the last trigger, until the next. why: a director's decisions (pack size, which place, which gesture) are drawn from expressions that keep moving, and a decision must not change inside a shot; today the only thing that holds is an integer bar count (`valueCount` holds a count, `valueLag` smooths, nothing holds a READING), so every such call is "by bar number only" and cannot read the track's level at the moment the shot began. design note first with what TouchDesigner (Hold CHOP, Trigger CHOP, Logic) and Notch (the Latch / Sample and Hold modifiers) offer, then the node: its state under seek, replay and reset (§V181's rule for stateful value nodes), what it publishes before the first trigger, a vector value. the consumer writes its own test on it.|T1561b,T1591b,V181
T1650b|.|**STOCK MAPS: WHAT §T1618b LEFT.** (1) a HELD map is addressed `uv × (size − 1)` truncated, so its last texel shows only at exactly 1 and a map spreads `size − 1` texels over 0..1; not changed because it would move every mapped picture — decide once, with the list of pictures it moves (Repeat and Mirror already use all `size` texels). (5) the preview tile shows neither a map nor the points' `uv`.|T1618b

CONSUMER DATA POINT (shaderloom-f1, in the app at 1280×720, documents back to back, twice, a loaded machine): five casting lights + 4× MSAA 26–30 fps; two casting + MSAA 34–42; two, no MSAA 45–54; one, no MSAA 52–58; no shadow, no focus, no MSAA 55–60. T1601b|.|**THE TESTS THAT WALK THE WHOLE NODE CATALOGUE HAVE NO NAME (found 2026-10-05: three reds reached main).** 26 test files outside `test:gates` enumerate every node definition (`src/agent/surface.test.ts`, `parameter-range.test.ts`, the help reference and panel, `definitions/index.test.ts`, `registry.test.ts`, `menus/schemas.test.ts`, …). under "tests follow the blast radius" a change to a node definition must run exactly these, and nothing told the worker or the lead which they are. wanted: a derived list, as `gate-list.test.ts` derives `test:gates` — a script `pnpm test:catalogue` whose membership a test checks (a test that iterates `allNodeDefinitions` or the registry's list and is not a GPU file belongs on it), named in CLAUDE.md's scoping ladder as the step for "a node definition changed". until then the list lives in the lead's scratchpad and in the worker rules.|T1586b,T1273,V957
T1600b|.|**A VALUE LOOP WITH A DELAY IN IT IS LEGAL, AND A REFUSED LOOP NAMES ITS PATH (from §T1561b, shaderloom-f1).** "an integrator whose rate depends on its own output" is every speed that depends on position, and it has no stock spelling: `rate → lag → speed → expression → rate` is dropped whole by the value graph (`valueGraph.cycle`: every member emits nothing), and a `valueDelay` in the loop does not break it. T1596b|.|**ONE PREVIEW TILE'S REFUSAL SHOULD NOT STARVE THE OTHERS (left by §B250).** `previews/system.ts` `tick()` returns one command for all tiles, and an orbit target with no declared matrix throws (a refusal with its own test, `synthesis-uniform-update.test.ts`), so a throw anywhere loses every tile's uniforms for that tick. since §B250 the compiler no longer produces the case; a hand-built request still does. wanted: the refusal becomes a per-tile diagnostic — skip that tile's orbit, keep the others, report it where the app can show it (the Problems registry, §T1555b), which needs a channel `tick()` does not have today.|B250,T1555b

T1713b|x|**E89 PLATE ENGINE: MODAL CHLADNI/BESSEL FIGURES (owner 2026-10-19, after the research pass in §T1712b).** A plate's figure is its forced response, Σ φᵢ(x)φᵢ(r₀)/(k²−kᵢ²+iγ) (Tuan et al. 2015): crisp at a resonance, smeared between, and those resonances are the mode spots the owner wants to stop on. Plan: a `Medium` switch (liquid | plate) in E89; mode amplitudes in a small Feedback loop that relax toward the forced-response target, so a sweep rings and crossfades; a field pass writing the liquid state's layout (height and its quadrature) so the strobe/mirror renderer, palettes and HUD read it unchanged; shapes: circle (Bessel J_m(j′ₘₙr)cos mθ, zeros computed at build time), square (Chladni ψ±), hexagon and triangle (hexagonal-lattice sums); drive as a ring of S sources selecting the symmetry. One vessel distance function shared by liquid walls, plate masks and renderer. BUILT 2026-10-19: `src/examples/shaders/cymatics-plate.ts` (tables computed at build: 210 circle modes with J′ zeros by Simpson + bisection, 391 square, 37 hexagon orbits), `CYMATICS_PLATE_MODES_WGSL` (Bessel by Miller recurrence, normalised modes, symmetric drives), `CYMATICS_PLATE_FIELD_WGSL` (field normalised by total modal amplitude), `switch_medium`, vessel `shape` 0..3 shared by liquid, plate, sand and camera. Known: the circle's high-m figures live near the rim (J_m at r > m/k), so its centre stays ringed.|T1712b
T1714b|x|**E89 SAND ON PLATES (after §T1713b).** Grains as GPU points that hop with a step ∝ the local vibration envelope and so collect on nodal lines in ~1000 cycles (Grabec & Sok 2023); fine powder drifts the other way (Faraday 1831; van Gerner 2010, Γ<1). Rendered as light grains on a black plate under raking light. BUILT 2026-10-19: four sand kernels × 1,000,000 grains (a Point Kernel caps at 1e6; each kernel its own random stream via `slot`, pictures summed by `add_sand`), six Grabec hops a frame with a drift down ∇A², powder reverses it, Scatter button), `points_sand` into a 2048² dish-space texture, lit in `wgsl_surface` (now `customWgslMulti`) as a heightmap under a raking light; reads `switch_medium`, so floating grains work on the liquid too. Gate rows: T900 digest + region count 75, kernel count 142 (`point-kernel-params.test.ts`). Broken sand lines were DAMPING, not grain count: the forced response is complex, and with heavy damping |z| vanishes at points, not along lines; plate damping now ships at 0.005, where one phase dominates and the nodal curves close.|T1713b
T1715b|~|**E89 LIQUID PRESETS AND SHAPES (after §T1714b).** Two-frequency Faraday recipes (4:5 twelve-fold quasipattern, Edwards & Fauve 1994; 6:7 superlattice, Kudrolli/Pier/Gollub 1998; 1:2 with phase), vessel shapes from 2D distance functions (hexagon, triangle, star, stadium, guitar outline), oil and mercury looks. BUILT 2026-10-19: vessel 4 = Faraday lattice drawn in `CYMATICS_PLATE_FIELD_WGSL` (order N plane waves + second ring at half a step + quadratic term; drawn, because the shallow-water liquid lacks the selecting nonlinearity), `presets_recipes` bank of ten recipes on the Panel. OPEN: oil and mercury looks; stadium/star/guitar outlines.|T1713b

T1718b|~|**E89 SAND IS A LAYER THAT SHIPS OFF (owner 2026-10-22: *"we dont change loom itself in hacky ways. we should definitely arrange the project in a way where we dont cook the sand and its dependents if they are not on"*).** BUILT, UNCOMMITTED. `toggle_sand` (a uniform the surface read, with every sand pass still cooking) is gone. `layer_sand` (blend Replace, opacity 1) stacks `wgsl_sandlit` (the surface plus the sand, `CYMATICS_SANDLIT_WGSL`) over `wgsl_surface` (`CYMATICS_SURFACE_WGSL`, now a `customWgsl` built from the same template without the sand parameters, binding, functions and mix: an unwired `inputTexture1` is refused at save). The §T1717b `awake` and size-0 gates are removed, so the kernel source is the committed one again (T900 digest back to `4de0890542928729`). Measured, Dawn/Metal 1920x1080, alternated: liquid (sand off) 17.06 → 8.70 ms; sand on 25.10 → 25.59 (a second surface pass and the layer). Byte-identical to the §T1717b build over 90 frames in liquid, sand on, and sand on a square plate. Switching the layer keeps the liquid's feedback state (hash unchanged across off and on) and re-seeds the sand (it scatters and gathers again). ⚑ GATE CHANGE, ruled by the owner 2026-10-22 (*"that rule is superseded then"*), recorded as §V1030: §V25's no-dead-nodes check (`runner.test.ts`) refused any Layer shipped off, which is why E82 ships its idle layers ON at opacity 0. It now holds a file with off Layers to the plan with them ON (`compileLayerWarmPlan`, exposed as `runExample().layersOn`): nothing but the unwireable may be pruned there, and the shipped plan may prune exactly that plus what the off Layers hide (the off Layer itself is spliced out of `order`). Thumbnail not regenerated.|T1717b,T1498b,T1507b,V25,V1030,T900

T1719b|~|**A COMPILED NODE HANDS BACK ITS VALUE FUNCTION: THE VALUES LANE WITHOUT RE-EMISSION (design `docs/value-functions-design-2026-11-03.md`, 2026-11-03; AWAITS THE OWNER'S REVIEW).** measured on sentinel-bot (the app's frame headless on the mock device, alternated against HEAD): the values-lane compile is 4.4 ms = resolving 41 nodes' parameters 2.0 + re-running `compile` for 48 nodes 2.0 + normalising, reading and comparing their passes 0.5; `render_shot` 0.60, `camera_rig` 0.35. wanted: `CompiledNodeDescription.values?: (inputs) => NodeFrameValues` — this frame's parameters, maps, scene payloads and time probe in; per-pass value fields (uniforms, a write's rows, a loop's count) and scene payloads out, with no field that can carry structure; `compileFrame` swaps value fields on the base passes, by reference everywhere else, instead of re-emitting and comparing. a node without one keeps today's path and §V936's verifier. proposed V1031 (values only, by reference), V1032 (`compile` fills its base values through the function it returns), V1033 (spliced through value functions = re-emitted = full compile, every shipped example, frames 1, 37, 240). slices: S1 seam + Level, S2 camera, S3 Render, S4 Point Kernel / Material WGSL / Custom WGSL, S5 measure E89, E55, E77, sentinel-bot. expected (an estimate): 2.5 ms to about 0.6 on sentinel-bot. the general form of §T1686b's ask; TD/Notch/Unreal comparison in the design's §2. **2026-11-03: S1 LANDED (uncommitted).** `CompiledNodeDescription.values` (`node-definition.ts`); `compile.ts` keeps it on the retained record when every pass emitted and the node publishes no scene payload yet; `compileFrame` swaps value fields onto the base passes (`passesWithValues`, `frame-compile.ts`), checking one entry per pass and each block's names against its base block (`isUniformValue` now exported from `plan.ts`). T1725b|.|**BLUR IS THE ENGINE'S LARGEST GPU COST ON SHIPPED EXAMPLES, AND EVERY WAY TO HALVE IT MOVES PIXELS: THE OWNER'S CALL (measured 2026-11-03).** `blurNode` (`filters.ts`) is a two-pass separable Gaussian with `ceil(3σ)` taps a side (σ = size/2), capped at 64: E55's size-42 blurs read 127 texels and evaluate `exp()` per pixel on each pass, about 230 M samples a blur a frame at 1280 × 720. Ablation on Dawn/Metal, alternated in one session: E55 at 720p 19.7–20.2 ms with its blurs, 15.6–15.7 ms with them at size 2 (22 % of the frame); Blur ranks first or second by GPU span on E55, E75, E76 and E77 (spans overlap on Apple GPUs, so they rank and do not sum). Options, none picture-identical: (a) LINEAR-SAMPLING TAP PAIRS — one bilinear fetch at the weight-centred offset for each adjacent pair: half the fetches; differs from today by the device's filtering precision; (b) PRE-SHRINK as TouchDesigner's Blur TOP has it (a parameter, default 0 = today's picture, so nothing moves unless a document asks); (c) precomputed weights in the uniform block instead of `exp()` per tap (small; float-level differences). TD comparison and §V147's exact claims both bear on which: (b) is free of picture risk by default and is TD's own shape; (a) speeds every document and re-derives every blur claim. NOT STARTED: the owner rules on (a)/(b)/(c) first.|T40,T147,V147,T1717b

T1739b|x|**ACCUMULATE SUB-FRAMES ON THE GPU.** `--spp` today reads back every sub-frame and averages in JS. The perfumery finals measured 3–10× the GPU's own cost (Currents 0.73 s wall against 0.06 s GPU per frame at 16 spp). An accumulate target, added in linear float and resolved once per output frame, reads back one frame instead of N. LANDED: `LoomBackend.accumulateOutput?(outputId, decode)` (required on `VgpuBackend`; `LinearDecode`/`OutputAccumulator`/`AccumulatedSum` in `backend-types.ts`), built in `src/runtime/backend/vgpu/output-accumulator.ts`: each `add` copies the output's STORED bytes into a buffer and one compute pass decodes every channel through the caller's tables, indexed by the raw pattern (a half's 16 bits, the byte, so an `-srgb` target decodes by the table and not the sampler's curve), and adds premultiplied linear light into an f32 sum per pixel; `read` is ONE counted readback, then a zero sum. The tables are `linearDecodeFor` (`offline-render.ts`), the ones `LinearAverager` reads, and both sums resolve through `resolveLinearSum`: the two paths agree bit for bit where alpha is 1 by construction (colour × 1 exact, one f32 add correctly rounded both sides). Harness: `accumulate { every, decode, onSum }` sums captured frames on the device; a `decode` of undefined reads each back to `onCapture` as before. `renderFrames` `averaging: "gpu"` (default) or `"cpu"` (the reference); `r32float`, or a sum past the device's storage binding (3840×2160 fits the default 128 MiB), sums on the CPU and says so. Tests (`offline-render.gpu.test.ts`), red-verified: E1 at spp 4, frames 30–31, GPU equals the CPU average in every channel with >1,000 fractional-alpha pixels a frame, from 2 readbacks against 8 (red: alpha weight dropped → 22,101 channels differ; each summed frame also read back → 10 readbacks); T1738b's sawtooth spp tests now run the GPU path, exact. Measured, perfumery-pillar-show 1 s at spp 8 `--quality final`, 1920×1080, CPU and GPU alternated in one process: CPU 0.641 and 0.769 s a frame, GPU 0.403 and 0.403 s (1.6–1.9×), readbacks 480 → 60, frames 0, 30 and 59 identical across the two. What remains (CPU profile, 12 frames): waiting on the GPU's own work (~1.8 s idle) and the CPU resolve (~100 ms a 1080p frame with the GPU idle): §T1746b.|T1738b

T1741b|x|**10-BIT VIDEO EXPORT.** The app records H.264 Baseline (`avc1.42001f`), 8-bit 4:2:0, which bands dark reds and greens into flat steps. That is the owner's "blotchy" on LED content. Offer HEVC Main 10 (and ProRes where the platform has it) as a recording format; keep H.264 as the compatible default. **LANDED 2026-11-08.** A recording format, picked in the Render dialog and set on the bus by `export.setRenderFormat {format}` (app session; take-local like the job's range and rate, so it resets when the dialog opens and is not persisted, as no render setting is; refused while a take runs). One table, `src/runtime/export/recording/video-format.ts`: `h264` (the default, unchanged: Baseline 4.2 through 1080p, High 5.2 above), `h264-high` (High at the lowest Table A-1 level), `hevc-main10` (`hvc1.2.4.L<Table A.8 level>.B0`; not `hvc1.2.6`, which Chrome reads as 8-bit Main, measured). TEN BITS END TO END: the canvas is 8-bit, so a 10-bit take captures no canvas; the recorder reads the Output through the export interface (§V48) at full precision and `yuv10.ts` converts it to BT.709 limited-range I420P10 (tagged bt709 / iec61966-2-1 / tv), handed to the encoder as an `I420P10` VideoFrame. An 8-bit Output (`rgba8unorm[-srgb]`, the default working format) is refused by name (`export.formatNeedsFloatOutput`), and the recorder's `start()` and the encoder refuse 8-bit input as well. MP4: `hvc1` sample entry with the encoder's `hvcC` (measured: array_completeness 1, key frames carry SEI and IDR only, so not `hev1`), no `avc1` brand, the mime type read from the record (`hevcCodecString`). WHY THE DEFAULT STAYS H.264: measured on macOS, Chrome 157 and Chromium 151 refuse `hvc1.2.4` in `isConfigSupported`; Chrome 157 encodes true Main 10 only when launched with `--enable-features=PlatformHEVCHbdEncoderSupport` (no chrome://flags entry), and the dialog's refusal names that switch and H.264 High. When the browser and the Output both refuse, the dialog names both. ProRes: WebCodecs has no ProRes encoder; `pnpm render` (§T1738b) writes it. TESTS (counts per file): `video-format` 10, `yuv10` 10, `mp4-muxer` 24 (+6 HEVC, on Chrome's measured hvcC), `webcodecs` 11 (+7), `recorder` 17 (+3), `render-range` 23 (+4), `use-render-range` 24 (+4; its fake transports also gained VN71's `resetState`, whose absence had 15 of its 20 red at HEAD), `render-video-dialog` 15 (+2). E2E `ten-bit-video.spec.ts` (chromium-gpu): the installed Chrome with the switch renders a dark float ramp both ways through `renderFrameRange`; ffprobe reads hevc / Main 10 / yuv420p10le / `hvc1`, the decoded luma shows 66 levels and lies within 1.5 codes of the BT.709 ramp (an 8-bit source cannot get under 1.72), against H.264's 18 levels and 48 px bands; the lane's own Chromium pins the default refusal. Red-verified with 12 mutations, among them quantising the converter to 8 bits (the e2e failed at 2.13 codes while ffprobe still said Main 10). Left: §T1748b (VP9 profile 2, the 10-bit encoder Chrome ships on), §T1749b (convert on the GPU).|T1738b

T1745b|x|**`pnpm render` STARTS COLD AT ITS FIRST FRAME (left by §T1738b).** A still at `--at T` and a clip from `--from T` step only their own frames, so feedback, trails, simulations and analyze channels start from cleared state there: E1's orb at 1 s renders without the trail the app shows. The scratch still path stepped one unseen frame; On Nothing's render has `--warm N` (output frames rendered unseen before the first). Decide the rule (a `--warm` seconds/frames flag, or a default from what the plan holds temporal) and gate it with a feedback example whose frame at T matches a render from 0. LANDED, the rule: A RENDER IS DETERMINISTIC FROM ITS WARM-UP'S FIRST FRAME. `temporalStateOf(plan, flattened graph, nodes)` (`offline-render.ts`) names what carries state, read off the compiled plan: a `pingPong` (feedback), a `ring` (history), a `bufferPair` (simulation), a target whose first draw of the frame does not clear (trails), an allocated Analyze reduction (the next frame reads it, §V144), and a value node declaring `stateful` (§V181). Default: a plan with any is warmed from the timeline's frame 0, so the frame at T is frame T of a render from 0; a plan with none is not warmed. `--warmup S` steps S seconds instead (clamped at frame 0, and said), `--warmup 0` starts cold. The warm-up steps at the render's own rate (spp × fps: a feedback steps once per sub-frame) and reads nothing back and sums nothing. Harness: `warmup(plan) → n` steps a run-up as frames −n … −1 from `startFrame − n`, never captured or probed; `betweenFrames` may return a promise, awaited, so a movie decoder prefetches through the run-up; a movie feed's "nothing shown yet" is no longer frame −1 (that frame uploaded zero bytes, a GPU validation error). A free-running movie starts at the warm-up's first frame. The command prints the warm-up's reason and length, and now prints the error findings that did not stop a render (it dropped them). Tests, red-verified: E1 `--at 1` warms 60 frames by default for `feedback "echo"` and equals frame 60 of a render from 0 (red: run-up not stepped → 199,704 channels differ; transport not moved back → 460,722); the disc at its LFO position at 1 s is opaque and identical warm and cold; its LFO position at 0.75 s (64 px back) is (0,0,0,0) cold and lit warm (red: that assertion); the ribbon is >5× the disc's cover. The stateless saw is not warmed and renders the same with 2 frames of warm-up (red: a carrier for every plan). A free-run movie with a one-frame warm-up starts at 0.125 s with no error finding (red: the old −1 sentinel; an offset that ignores the run-up). Left: several `--at` times on a stateful plan each warm from 0 (§T1747b).|T1738b
T1746b|.|**THE `--spp` RESOLVE RUNS ON THE CPU WHILE THE GPU WAITS (left by §T1739b).** The sum is on the GPU and read once per output frame, but `resolveLinearSum` (mean, un-premultiply, `linearToSrgb` three times a pixel, round to 16 bits) runs in script: ~100 ms a 1080p frame, measured on perfumery-pillar-show at spp 8 `--quality final` (1.28 s of a 5.6 s profile of 12 frames), with the GPU idle meanwhile, and the CPU idle ~1.8 s waiting on the GPU. Overlap the two: resolve frame N in slices between frame N+1's sub-frame steps (its emission waits a group), or resolve on the GPU into 16-bit values, held to a stated tolerance against `resolveLinearSum` (an f32 `pow` is not the f64 one). Bit-exactness between `averaging: "gpu"` and `"cpu"` holds today because both resolve here; keep the CPU reference whichever is chosen.|T1739b
T1747b|.|**SEVERAL `--at` STILLS ON A STATEFUL PLAN EACH WARM UP FROM 0 (left by §T1745b).** `pnpm render --at 10,20,30` renders each still in its own run, and each warms from frame 0 by default, so it steps 60 s of warm-up where one run that captured each still on its way would step 30. Render the times of one command in one run, in time order, capturing (and summing, at `--spp`) each still's sub-frames where it falls; a stateless plan keeps the per-still runs, which step nothing they do not need.|T1745b

Measured 2026-11-08 (Chrome 157 and Chromium 151, macOS): `vp09.02.10.10` passes `isConfigSupported` (software libvpx), and I420P10 frames decode as yuv420p10le Profile 2 with 126 of a 128-code ramp intact. T1749b|.|**CONVERT A 10-BIT TAKE TO I420P10 ON THE GPU (left by §T1741b).** A 10-bit take reads every frame back as rgba16float (8 bytes per pixel) and converts it in JS: measured 18.5 ms per frame at 1080p and 73 ms at UHD for the conversion alone, where the 8-bit canvas path reads nothing back (about 60 fps at UHD, `experiments/canvas-export`). A compute pass writing BT.709 limited-range 10-bit planes into a buffer would read back 3 bytes per pixel and drop the CPU pass. a scale inside the analysis needs a site per consumer + a port message to the audio thread, & the fallback would be the one forgotten. as an `AudioParam` it ramps sample-accurately on the audio thread. **(2) CLIPPING:** the graph carries floats ∴ a trimmed signal above full scale passes unclipped; said in both descriptions. **(3) MONITOR:** a live input was never routed to the speakers & still is not (source → trim → analysis, nothing else) ∴ no gain can feed back or be heard. a file's monitor USED TO hang off the analyser's output (= the source @ unity); the analyser now sits behind the trim ∴ the monitor is tapped off the SOURCE: two branches, source → trim → analysis & source → volume → speakers. +48 dB of trim moves no loudspeaker; Volume still moves no channel. **(4) LIVE, NO RESTART (microphone):** read per frame in `sync` through the one read path (`resolvedInputGainDb` → `resolveParameters`, §V61) ∴ expression / preset fade / Panel all drive it; sent as ONE `setTargetAtTime` (τ = 20 ms, `INPUT_GAIN_SMOOTHING_SECONDS`: a step in gain is a step in the signal the onset detectors would count) only when the value moved; deliberately ⊥ ∈ `captureKeyOf` for a mic ∴ the device is never reopened. Jacobi like every hook read: the gain a frame resolves is heard by the next frame's analysis. **(5) `audioFileIn` GETS IT TOO, UNDER THE SAME NAME, BUT READ AT REST:** a locked file's features are a PRE-ANALYSED TRACK, walked at one gain (the byte map's truncation & clamp make a post-hoc gain on recorded features inexact) ∴ for a file it rides `CaptureConfig.inputGainDb` into the capture key & `preAnalysisKey`, exactly like Hit Threshold: a change restarts the capture & re-analyses. the description says so. **(6) OFFLINE = THE APP:** `analyseOffline(…, inputGainDb)` multiplies its OWN float32 copy of the decoded samples by `inputGainLinear` (10^(dB/20), the one conversion, `audio-analysis-protocol.ts`) before the hop engine, the tonal pass & the tuning estimate; the worker request, the main-thread fallback, `pnpm render` (`audioFeed` in `src/tooling/offline-render.ts`, from the same `captureConfigOf`; its note names a non-zero gain & a non-static one is listed as read at rest) & the shipped-clip stand-in (`src/examples/shipped-clip-audio.ts`) all pass it. the PCM an export carries is the caller's array, never written ∴ unity. **(7) LEDGERS: unchanged, checked.** `NODE_REPRODUCIBILITY` (`audioIn` external-live, `audioFileIn` pure) & `NODE_SIDE_EFFECTS` are per node type; a stored number read at rest keeps a locked file `f(frame)`. feature-track `provenance` does ⊥ record the gain (a mic's moves during a take; a track replays the numbers it recorded, §V352) — §T1777b. NO `FEATURE_TRACK_VERSION` bump: 0 dB is the samples untouched, every existing reading is what it was. **TD/NOTCH:** TD's Audio Device In CHOP has no gain; the idiom is a Math CHOP (or Audio Filter) between the device & Audio Spectrum / Analyze — a multiply ahead of the analysis in a graph where audio is a first-class signal. Notch's sound-reactive modifiers carry their own gain/scale per modifier. Loom has no audio-rate wire: the analysis lives inside the capture & only FEATURES cross into the value graph, so *"put a Math before the analyser"* has no place to stand, & a gain AFTER it (a Math on a band) cannot recover a floored band — that would be the workaround. the trim on the source IS the TD idiom's multiply, at the only point in Loom where the signal exists; structural (constraints are fixed at open) ∴ ∈ `CaptureConfig` & `captureKeyOf` — flipping it reopens the device, said in the description. **A CONSTRAINT IS A REQUEST:** after opening, `track.getSettings()` is read back & `captureProcessingMessage` names on the Audio capture status line any stage the browser KEPT against the request & any it does ⊥ REPORT (unknown ≠ off), §V288; the capture still runs. **TD/NOTCH & audio tools:** TD's Audio Device In & Notch read the driver's stream as delivered (CoreAudio / ASIO / WASAPI) & expose device, rate, channels — no AGC / NS / AEC switch; OS-level voice processing is something a DAW user turns OFF in the OS (Windows *audio enhancements*, macOS mic modes). conferencing tools are where the three are on by default. Loom is the first kind ∴ raw default, & the single switch is the one concession to the browser being a conferencing runtime. **EXISTING DOCUMENTS:** no stored data changes shape (the parameter is absent = OFF). a file saved before this that listens on a microphone now hears the RAW device: quieter on average where AGC was boosting (use Input Gain, §T1769b), w/ a WIDER dynamic range, sustained material & percussion no longer gated, & the room's own playback no longer subtracted — gains / thresholds tuned against the processed signal will need retuning. that is the intended fix; a document that wants the old behaviour sets Voice Processing on. ⟶ **LANDED 2026-11-12, uncommitted.** `src/app/audio-capture-config.ts` (`captureAudioConstraints`, `captureProcessingMessage`, `CAPTURE_PROCESSING_STAGES`, `CaptureConfig.voiceProcessing`), `src/app/use-audio-input.ts`, `src/nodes/definitions/audio.ts`; `src/app/audio-capture-processing.test.tsx` (10, the real hook over a recording `getUserMedia` whose track's `getSettings()` the test sets): the constraints of every call `toEqual` (default, chosen device, fallback, switch on), the flip stops the old stream & asks again, the status sentence for a kept stage & an unreported one; `src/tests/e2e/audio-input-gain.spec.ts` gains: the one real `getUserMedia` call was asked `{ audio: { echoCancellation: false, noiseSuppression: false, autoGainControl: false } }` & this Chromium's fake-device track read back w/ nothing to name. T1806b|.|**THE MUSIC FEATURES CONTRACT, WHAT §T1805b LEFT ROUGH (each changes what a consumer reads, so not changed in the promotion; decide, then change both components & silk's mapping together).** (1) MIDI `voiceNEnvelope` reaches 1.2: the pedal gain `0.7 + 0.5 sustain - 0.35 soft` is applied inside; audio's is 0..1. (2) `tension` rests at 0.074 (audio, `0.2 * (1 - G)` through the curve) & 0.017 (MIDI, span term at the rest pitches), not 0. (3) an empty MIDI role reads pitch 48/54/60/66/72 & velocity 0.5; audio reads 0 for an unknown pitch. (4) `sensitivity` is 0..2 default 1 on MusicFeatures, 0..1 default 0.5 on MidiFeatures (touch curve). (5) `chordIndex`: audio counts accepted changes of the chord count; MIDI also counts the chord ENDING, and a chord struck inside the hold-off after one ended is not sampled (roles keep the rest pitches until the next accepted change). (6) audio voices 2..4 are fifth / extension / top note: under a plain triad three voices share a pitch class. (7) `kickFast` 0.12 on the first kick of a bar whose level drops; `snare` 0 on Audio Pattern while `snareFast` fires (the slow presence gate `gs`). (8) `noteDensity` is 0..5 from audio (tracked notes), unbounded from MIDI (ringing keys). NOT STARTED.

T1301|.|**E57 FOREST — THE BEAT-DRIVEN LIGHT *BLINKS* & IT IS UGLY; & THE MOON APPEARS TO BOUNCE W/ THE WALK.** owner: *"the forest example is super ugly with the blinking of the light to the music. that's not gonna work like this like at all. and also should the moon bounce up and down while walking? i think that shouldn't move as much as the trees with each step."* **TWO SEPARATE THINGS & they want separate answers.** ⚑**(a) THE BLINK IS §T1279's `moonGain = dimMap1.lowMid · (1 − 0.3·kickCount)` — A KICK ON EVERY BEAT DIPPING THE SCENE'S PRIMARY LIGHT @ 112 BPM = the whole picture pulsing ~2×/s, which is what \"blinking\" means.** §T1279 was built to the owner's OWN brief (*"dim the light… some beats and some rhythm"*) & the STILLS looked right — **a per-frame still cannot show a blink; only motion can, & the owner is the first to have WATCHED it.** ∴ the row's fix is a LOOK CALL & the options differ ∈ kind: (i) take the beat OFF the primary light entirely & put it on something that can flash w/o the scene strobing (the SHAFTS already carry `snareCount`; the glints; a rim), (ii) keep the dip but make it a SLOW SWELL rather than a per-beat step (the count rests @ 0 & decays over 250 ms — lengthen the release ∨ drive from a LEVEL rank instead of a HIT count, which §T1279 itself says is the difference between something that LANDS & something that BREATHES: the owner asked for LAND & got STROBE), (iii) drop the moon dip & keep only the fog gloom on onsets. RECOMMEND (i)+(iii) — the primary light of a night scene is the one thing that ! ⊥ flicker. ⚑**(b) THE MOON: THE CODE SAYS IT CANNOT MOVE & THAT ! BE MEASURED BEFORE IT IS BELIEVED.** `bob`/`sway` are TRANSLATIONS of the eye (`:867` docblock: *"the moon, the quiet zone and the per-pixel sky direction hold exactly as still as they did before"*) & the camera basis is built from `pitch` ALONE (`:906-909`: `fwd`/`right`/`upv` do ⊥ read the eye) ∴ the per-pixel ray direction is INDEPENDENT of eye position & a disc @ infinity is SCREEN-STATIC BY CONSTRUCTION. **so either the owner is seeing something ELSE move (the veil, the glow, trees OCCLUDING & REVEALING the disc as they parallax — which would read as the moon flickering ∨ jumping), ∨ the docblock asserts a fact that is ⊥ true — & THIS REPO HAS SHIPPED EXACTLY THAT TWICE TONIGHT (§B202, §T1284's twin).** MEASURE IT: render a stride's worth of frames, find the moon disc's SCREEN CENTROID per frame, & report its excursion ∈ pixels next to a NEAR TRUNK's excursion over the same frames. if the moon's is ~0 the docblock is right & the fix is whatever else is moving; if it is ⊥, the docblock is wrong & that is the bug. **⊥ A GUESS EITHER WAY — the number decides.** owner: shaderloom-d0 owns E57 but is mid-§T1283 stage 3; the MEASUREMENT half is diagnostic & can be taken by anyone|T1279,T1170b,B202,V903,V147 ⇒ **(b) MEASURED, & THE DOCBLOCK IS TRUE: THE MOON DISC DOES ⊥ MOVE. A ~7,500:1 RATIO.** & the moon's 0.03 px is ⊥ even eye motion: decomposed against the gait's own frequencies it is per-STEP 0.002 px, per-STRIDE 0.013, slow-trend 0.037 — a MONOTONIC DRIFT, i.e. the `veil` noise re-shading the disc's brightness gradient. sanity check passed before trusting the blob: 63×65 px measured against 64 px predicted from `moonSize` 3.2° @ `lens` 1.45, centre (764.5, 192.5) against the analytic projection (764, 194) ∴ it IS the disc, ⊥ a glow ∨ a shaft. ⚑**WHAT IS ACTUALLY MOVING: A THIN TRUNK STANDS DIRECTLY ∈ FRONT OF THE DISC & SLIDES ACROSS IT AS YOU WALK.** the disc's VISIBLE area swings 2143 → 2434 → 2143 px against 3270 unoccluded ∴ **27–34 % of the moon is hidden @ ALL times & that fraction BREATHES by ±7 % of the disc per stride**; T947|.|**LASER & OSCILLOSCOPE EXAMPLES — & THEY ARE THE SAME THING. owner: *spec out a laser simulation example as well as an oscilloscope simulation example… research common lasers and how they are driven, if they can be network driven, and then maybe implement one node for the most popular one to prove we can go from visualization to actual driving production hardware just as touchdesigner would*.** ⚑**BOTH ARE XY VECTOR DISPLAYS: a scope ∈ X-Y mode IS a vector display; a laser projector IS an XY GALVO SCANNER. ∴ ONE simulation path — 2 value channels (X,Y) + blanking + colour → a persistent-phosphor trace — & 2 DRESSINGS**: scope = CRT phosphor (green, decay, bloom); laser = beam divergence + scan-rate artifacts + a REAL OUTPUT. ⊥ build 2 examples that share nothing. ⚑⚑**THE PHYSICS THAT MAKES BOTH LOOK REAL, & it is ONE FACT: BRIGHTNESS IS A FUNCTION OF *DWELL TIME*.** a galvo ∨ CRT beam moving SLOWLY deposits more energy ∴ **CORNERS ARE BRIGHT ∵ THE BEAM DECELERATES**, & fast strokes are dim. that is why real laser art has hot dots @ path vertices — & drawing a constant-brightness polyline is EXACTLY what makes a fake one look fake. same family as §T940's *dust is the mechanism*. **+ SCAN RATE (points/second, e.g. 30k pps) BOUNDS HOW MUCH GEOMETRY FITS BEFORE FLICKER** ∴ simulating it honestly GIVES the characteristic wobble & flicker rather than needing them faked. **HARDWARE = §T942's BRIDGE, ⊥ a new transport**: Ether Dream is TCP + UDP discovery, IDN is UDP ∴ **a page cannot reach either & this is a CONCRETE DRIVER for the device bridge rather than a separate ask.** RESEARCH: which DAC TD supports best (⚠**I BELIEVE TD has an Etherdream CHOP — VERIFY, ⊥ assume**), Ether Dream vs Helios vs LaserCube vs Pangolin FB4, the ILDA DB25 analog standard & **IDN as the modern open network standard**, & what SAFETY the output path !
